messages:
mia: Heads up — we just had a layering surprise: a canary ended up routing ~100% of traffic for ~2m. Need to align on precedence rules for flags vs rollout policies. :grimacing:
sam: Yikes. Can you paste the rollout + flag snippets? Is this from Console or runtime overrides?
mia: Console rollout created a 1% canary, but a runtime flag was flipped that had a higher priority. Snippet:```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","rollout":{"canary":1,"variant":"v2"},"runtime_flags":{"generate.v2_override":100}}
```
deploy-bot: deploy completed: service/api@2026-03-20T09:12Z (canary=1%)
zach: If the runtime flag is a direct traffic knob (percent) it will naturally override. But we never agreed on explicit tie-break rules between 'runtime flag traffic' and 'rollout split'.
anita: We intentionally separated concerns: rollout = gradual deploy, flags = feature toggles. But who has last-say for traffic splitting is ambiguous. I think rollouts should be authoritative for deployment safety.
sam: Quick proposal: precedence order = emergency overrides (ops), explicit runtime flags marked "force" (temporal), rollout config (console), default model routing. That would make force-flags highest. But we need guard rails.
zach: Problem is we treat some runtime flags as feature toggles and some as traffic gates. We need metadata on flags: "type": "gate|feature|force" and the router enforces semantics.
mia: Agreed. Also want a safety check: disallow runtime flags to route >X% unless an approver grants a bypass. Minimal change: block any runtime flag that would push a route above 20% w/o approval.
anita: Okay but ops needs a way to emergency-cut. So "force" flags with audit+ttl should bypass the guard.
ops-bot: Policy check failed for flag toggle generate.v2_override by sam at 1855123123 — would route 100% (>20%) — blocked.
sam: Nice — where does that guard live? Console validation, runtime router, or flag service?
zach: Prefer runtime router enforcement so it's effective at request time and prevents race conditions between services. Console should show the validation result.
mia: Action items: 1) add "flag.type" enum and metadata to flag API (zach) 2) implement runtime router guard for >20% threshold with approver flow (sam + anita) 3) console shows blocked toggles + reason (mia)
anita: I'll draft a short RFC for the approval UX and emergency bypass flow.
sam: I'll pick up the router guard PR after the RFC.
zach: I'll add the flag metadata and update the flag-service schema.
mia: Thanks — for immediate mitigation I rolled back the runtime toggle and re-deployed canary-only. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollback completed: service/api@2026-03-20T09:15Z
mia: Leaving this here as a follow-up thread for the rollout/flag precedence doc — thanks everyone. :eyes:
